description: A nullish default keeps a real zero stock count where an or default would replace it
code:
stock = 0
count = stock ?? 10
legacy = stock || 10
assert(count, 0)
assert(legacy, 10)
stock = null
assert(count, 10)
assert(legacy, null)
count

description: Chained nullish defaults pick the first known nickname and follow later changes
code:
nick = null
name = null
label = nick ?? name ?? "guest"
assert(label, "guest")
name = "Ana"
assert(label, "Ana")
nick = "Annie"
assert(label, "Annie")
label

description: A class rule defaults each order's missing coupon and a callback lists the live discounts
code:
class Order(total, coupon):
    this.total = total
    this.coupon = coupon
$Order.discount = $Order.coupon ?? 0
first = Order(50, null)
second = Order(80, 15)
discounts = Order.map(order => order.discount)
assert(discounts, [0, 15])
first.coupon = 5
second.coupon = null
assert(discounts, [5, 0])
discounts

description: The right operand of a nullish default runs only once the left value is missing
code:
calls = []
def fallback():
    calls.push("fallback")
    return "default"
setting = "custom"
value = setting ?? fallback()
assert(value, "custom")
assert(calls, [])
setting = null
assert(value, "default")
assert(calls, ["fallback"])
value

description: A nullish default inside a callback replaces null readings without settling the list to null
code:
readings = [3, null, 5]
filled = readings.map(reading => reading ?? 0)
assert(filled, [3, 0, 5])
readings = [null, 2]
assert(filled, [0, 2])
filled

description: A class-level condition with a nullish default decides for devices without a profile
code:
class Device
if $Device.profile ?? false:
    $Device.mode = "managed"
else:
    $Device.mode = "open"
phone = Device()
assert(phone.mode, "open")
phone.profile = "corp"
assert(phone.mode, "managed")
phone.mode
